subject: Re: Post-call: Deployment mode & data isolation (Dedicated vs Private VPC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Alan / Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciated the context on FinSecure's production timelines and the compliance bar you're targeting. Quick recap + proposed next steps below.

Call recap:
- Primary requirement: strict customer data isolation for PII & transaction logs, expectation of no co-tenancy at the network level (controls on ingress/egress).
- KMS requirements: BYOK with customer-controlled keys preferred; HSM integration is a plus.
- Audit & evidence: SOC 2, detailed network diagrams, and retention/audit log access required for procurement.

Where Redwood's deployment modes map to this:
- Hosted API: fastest to prod but multi-tenant control plane and shared compute; not aligned with your network isolation ask.
- Dedicated: dedicated GPU pools (no shared compute), optional dedicated capacity, and customer isolation at the compute layer; control plane and networking remain hosted and multi-tenant — acceptable for many customers but not full network/VPC isolation.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full VPC isolation, customer-managed networking, optional on-prem package, and integrations for customer KMS/HSM — this is the strongest fit for your stated needs.

Attachments: Redwood_Data_Isolation_Summary.pdf (high-level mapping of Dedicated vs Private VPC + example network diagrams), SOC2_evidence_summary.xlsx (summary of controls we can share).

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm if FinSecure requires private VPC-level isolation (no shared networking) as a must-have, or if dedicated compute with strict tenancy controls would suffice?
2) If private VPC is required, we'd like to schedule a 30-min technical deep dive with Mateo (SE) to walk through network diagrams and BYOK flows.
3) I'll attach the procurement checklist and a rough timeline for Private VPC provisioning after you confirm.

If helpful, I can include pricing delta estimates for Dedicated vs Private VPC in the follow-up.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
m: 415-555-0192
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Network isolation: this is a hard requirement. We cannot have any possibility of cross-customer network access. That rules out multi-tenant networking; compute-level isolation (dedicated GPUs) is not sufficient on its own.
- KMS: we require BYOK and ability to rotate keys on our schedule. HSM-backed keys will be required for production.
- Control plane access: we need a model where audit logs and admin access are scoped to our org; other customers should not be visible in control-plane metadata.

Based on that, sounds like Private VPC (or on-prem) is what we should plan for. Can you confirm: does Redwood's Private VPC option support BYOK/HSM today, and do you have a short checklist we can send to procurement?

Also can Mateo join a technical session early next week? Sofia and I are available Mon/Tue mornings PST.

Thanks,
Alan
VP of Engineering

Alan — thanks for the quick clarification and the clear list of must-haves.

Short answers up front: yes, Private VPC supports BYOK/HSM integrations (we've completed integrations with several KMS providers and support customer-provided HSMs for key wrapping). Private VPC also provides fully customer-managed networking (no shared VPCs), and audit logs can be exported to your systems — access is scoped per-customer.

Additional detail: Dedicated (reserved capacity) provides dedicated GPU pools and isolation at the compute level: no other customers share the same GPU instances. However:
- The control plane for Dedicated in our hosted model remains multitenant (metadata about deployments lives in Redwood's control plane).
- Network-level isolation (VPC peering or customer-managed subnets) is available only with Private VPC or on-prem deployments.

What that means for procurement: if "no shared networking" and BYOK/HSM are non-negotiable, Private VPC or on-prem is the right path. Dedicated can be acceptable if procurement and security are satisfied with compute isolation + contractual guarantees and if you can live with Redwood-hosted control plane.

I've attached the Data Isolation Summary and SOC2 sheet again. I'll also prepare a procurement checklist (what we need for statement of work, network details, KMS vendor, and firewall rules).

Next steps: Mateo — can you run a 30-min technical deep dive on Mon 30 Mar 2026 at 09:30 AM PST? (Alan / Sofia confirmed Mon/Tue mornings). Mateo, if you prefer a different time please propose.

Alan / Sofia — I can also prepare a short one-page comparison doc that you can share with procurement.

Best,
Marissa
